title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages of the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes). There is a set or category M of 'pieces' X. Each piece has an 'external support' |X| and an 'internal support' |X|°, both subsets of an ambient space P. A 'notion' 𝔉 is a family of 'figures' F, each a set of pieces; 'majorée dans 𝔉' means contained in some figure. From the proof one infers that the |X|° for X in F are pairwise disjoint and that |F| is their union. Two pieces are disjoint when |Z|°∩|Y|°=∅; the page writes Z|∘|Y for disjoint and Z|·|Y for 'meets'. For 𝔏⊂M, supp°(𝔏) is the set of Y such that every Z disjoint from 𝔏 is also disjoint from Y. In modern terms this is the double polar 𝔏^{⊥⊥} for the disjointness relation, i.e. a Birkhoff/Galois closure. Σ_M is the lattice of such closed sets, an analogue of the algebra of regular open sets. The map φ sends A to the union of |X|° over X in A.

Definitions. The previous page defines a 'constructible internal support' as supp°(𝔏) with 𝔏 majorized by a figure. It then calls the support functor X↦|X| 'pleinement fidèle' for 𝔉 if, for every F in 𝔉, φ(cosupp°(F)) = P∖|F|. Grothendieck first wrote X and corrected it to P. This means P∖|F| is the union of the |Z|° over pieces Z disjoint from F. Equivalently, every point x outside |F| has a 'neighbourhood' |Z|° containing x and avoiding |F|. A marginal note says this property implies fidelity.

Proposition. For 𝔏⊂F, φ(supp°𝔏) = |𝔏|°, the union of the |X|° for X in 𝔏.

Proof.
- ⊇: since 𝔏⊂supp°𝔏, we get |𝔏|° ⊂ φ(supp°𝔏).
- ⊆: argue by contraposition. Suppose |Y|° meets the complement of |𝔏|°. We must produce Z disjoint from 𝔏 but meeting Y, which shows Y∉supp°𝔏.
- Case (i): |Y|° meets |F|∖|𝔏|° = |F∖𝔏|°. Then some Z in F∖𝔏 has |Z|° meeting |Y|°, and Z is disjoint from 𝔏 because the pieces of F are disjoint.
- Case (ii): |Y|° meets P∖|F|. Full faithfulness gives Z with x∈|Z|°⊂P∖|F|, so Z meets Y and is disjoint from |𝔏|°⊂|F|.

Purpose. On the next page this yields that 𝔏↦supp°𝔏 from 𝔓(F) to Σ_M commutes with Inf, Sup and relative complement. Hence the constructible supports subordinate to one figure form a Boolean algebra that maps homomorphically into 𝔓(P). This is the first step toward a combinatorial, point-free 'tame topology' in which constructible sets are reconstructed from pieces and the disjointness relation.
errors: Case (i) silently uses that the internal supports of the pieces of a figure F are pairwise disjoint and that |F| is their union, so that |F|∖|𝔏|° = |F∖𝔏|° and pieces of F∖𝔏 are disjoint from 𝔏. This hypothesis is not stated on the page.
Case (ii) needs the point x to lie in |Y|°∖|F|; this is given, so the argument is fine. Writing X instead of P is a slip that Grothendieck himself corrects ('ou plutôt P').
Notational sloppiness: F is used both for the figure and for an element of 𝔉, and |F| versus |F|° is not consistently distinguished.

ideas.what: Internal support supp°(𝔏) defined as the double orthogonal of 𝔏 for the disjointness relation among pieces; Σ_M is the lattice of such closed sets
ideas.modern_name: Polarity / Galois-closure lattice of an orthogonality relation; analogue of the regular-open Boolean algebra

ideas.what: 'Full faithfulness' of the support functor: the complement of a figure's support is covered by interiors of pieces disjoint from it
ideas.modern_name: Separation / local-basis condition (pieces form a basis for complements of constructible closed sets)
ideas.usually_credited_to: No standard name; akin to regularity conditions in tame topology / o-minimal cell decompositions

ideas.what: For a subfamily of a figure, the combinatorially defined support realizes geometrically to exactly the union of its strata. Consequence: subfigures of one figure form a Boolean algebra embedded in Σ_M and in 𝔓(P)
ideas.modern_name: Boolean algebra of constructible (definable) sets generated by a stratification/cell decomposition
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (constructible sets, Chevalley); in tame topology van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn (1980s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un Programme (1984) calls for 'tame topology' but gives no such formalism

missed.claim: An axiomatic, point-free framework for tame topology: pieces with internal and external supports, an orthogonality-closure lattice Σ_M, and a 'pleine fidélité' axiom guaranteeing that combinatorial supports realize correctly. This is a concrete fragment of Grothendieck's 1986 attempt at the 'topologie modérée' of the Esquisse, never developed in the literature in this form.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could be compared with o-minimal / definable-set frameworks and with locale-theoretic approaches. It documents how Grothendieck intended to recover constructible-set Boolean algebras from a disjointness relation on 'pieces'. The mathematics on this page itself is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The proof is an elementary lattice/topology argument. Its interest is only as a documented step in Grothendieck's unpublished 1986 axiomatization of tame topology via disjointness polarities, which is not in the literature but not deep either.
transcription_corrections: The page header is '77' and the next page is '78', so the previous page's header '78' is likely a misreading (probably 76).
The encircled 'X' in 'X∖|F|' is corrected by Grothendieck in the margin with the arrow note 'ou plutôt P'. The ambient set is P, not a piece X.
In the proof line 'Z|∘|𝔏, et Z|∘|Y', the second relation is a different symbol (Z|·|Y, 'meets'), as the explanation '|Z|°∩|Y|°≠∅' confirms.
Right margin note reads roughly 'Se rappeler que cette propriété implique la fidélité' (uncertain).
Left slanted margin note reads roughly 'explicitation de l'énoncé de validité 𝔏→|𝔏|°, ... en termes de figures' (uncertain).
In case (i), the underbrace should read '= |F∖𝔏|°'.
Case (ii) reads 'P∖|F|', consistent with the P correction.
